_comment: The only per-repo file in this skill. SKILL.md and repos.md are identical
across every repo that uses /ai-dev — when you copy the skill to another
project, edit this file and nothing else.
'toolkit' is the shared UI library this repo consumes from sources via a
relative path. Set it to null in a repo that has no such dependency.
runInstructions: BOTH scripts below end in `wait` and block until interrupted. Background them
(run_in_background, or `… &`) and poll the URL until it answers. Running one in
the foreground hangs you until you time out, with nothing verified.
Full app:
LUNICLE_PORT={port} LUNICLE_LOCAL_DATA=/tmp/ai-dev/{key} ./scripts/run-dev.sh --no-open
Demo — a different script AND a different port variable:
LUNICLE_DEMO_PORT={port} ./scripts/run-demo.sh --no-open
then browse http://127.0.0.1:{port}/?demo=1 — keep the query string or you get the
real app talking to a server that is not there. For a pure-frontend change this is
much faster: no JVM, no database, no sign-in, and you are a project-owner admin.
After an edit, rebuild :web:jsBrowserDevelopmentExecutableDistribution and reload —
no restart. Do NOT run both scripts at once; they are two ways to see the same
change and you have been assigned one port.
The port variables are isolation, not decoration, and each script has its own name
for it — LUNICLE_PORT for run-dev.sh, LUNICLE_DEMO_PORT for run-demo.sh. Neither
falls back to the other, and both scripts REFUSE to start on a port already held,
so leaving the demo on its 8081 default means the second concurrent ticket fails
outright. LUNICLE_LOCAL_DATA matters for the same reason: without it every worktree
shares ~/.lunicle/, where a worktree carrying a newer migration poisons the database
for the others.
Browse http://127.0.0.1:{port}/ — NOT localhost. A stale HttpOnly cookie on the
localhost host makes sign-in impossible to script. Sign in by setting
document.cookie = "lunicle_session=<id>; path=/" from a row in the sessions table.
Never run the real OAuth flow.
Stop whatever you started: ./scripts/stop-all.sh
